title: A Revised Digestion Method to Characterize Manganese Content in Solids
author: Ducret, Barbeau
materials: The optimized digestion method was tested to digest other metal oxides (purchased from Sigma‒Aldrich, USA) that have been commonly found in drinking water systems, such as Fe3O4 (95 % purity) [20], CuO (98 % purity) [21], Cu2O (97 % purity) [21] and Al(OH)3 (reagent grade) [22]. Fe, Al and Cu oxide standards were digested, filtered and immediately analyzed (with a limit of quantification of 20 µg Fe/L, 50 µg Cu/L and 1 mg Al/L) using flame atomic absorption (PinAAcle™ 900F, PerkinElmer, USA).

The solid content of each sample was harvested by filtration using a 2 µm filter (RAWG04700, MF-Millipore™) and then dried at 60 °C (the filter does not support heating at temperatures greater than 75 °C) for 48 h. As these filters are made from nitrocellulose membrane, they are fully dissolved in concentrated nitric acid or hydrochloric acid. Each sample was then digested in duplicate with the optimized HCl and EPA3050B methods. For each metal, the bias between both methods was calculated using Eq. (1).

steps.title: Weigh solid sample
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 0.5 g of dry solid and transfer it into an acid‑ and heat‑resistant digestion tube (e.g., metal‑free polypropylene cup).

steps.title: Add concentrated HCl
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL of concentrated HCl (12.4 M) to the tube at room temperature.

steps.title: Digest at high temperature
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a HotBlock® digestion system, cover with a ribbed watch glass to limit evaporation, and digest for 2.5 h at 95 °C under a chemical hood.

steps.title: Cool the digest
steps.instruction: Allow the digested samples to cool to room temperature for approximately 1 h.

steps.title: Dilute to final volume
steps.instruction: Dilute each cooled digest with Milli‑Q water to a final volume of 50 mL.

steps.title: Filter the solution
steps.instruction: Filter the diluted solution through a 2 µm composite PTFE‑polypropylene membrane (Filtermate™, SC0401, Delta Scientific) to remove insoluble material (e.g., silica particles).

steps.title: Analyze by atomic absorption
steps.instruction: Analyze the filtrate immediately by flame atomic absorption (e.g., PinAAcle™ 900F, PerkinElmer) for manganese (or other target metals).
